requirements.text: Put a frog in the toilet
requirements.source_phrase: Put a frog in the toilet

outcomes.description: Add a frog inside the toilet.
outcomes.target: A frog is visibly placed within the toilet bowl.
outcomes.reference: The toilet in the input image.

nodes.question: Is a recognizable frog visible in the toilet bowl opening or directly at its rim?
nodes.criteria: Pass if a recognizable frog is visible within the bowl opening or directly at its rim. Fail if that region is assessable and contains no recognizable frog. Unknown if frog identity or visibility of that region is insufficient. Identify the candidate and its visible location; this check does not establish that the frog is inside the bowl or that the request is complete.
nodes.binding: Inspect the edited image using the source toilet as the reference. Distinguish the bowl opening and rim from the raised lid, tank, surrounding fixtures, and floor. Frogs exclusively on those other surfaces do not pass this check.

nodes.question: Does comparison with the source show an added frog placement that constitutes progress toward putting a frog inside this toilet bowl?
nodes.criteria: Pass if source comparison establishes a newly added frog inside the bowl, or a visibly incomplete placement into the bowl such as a frog straddling the rim with part of its body extending into the interior. Describe whether the observed placement appears inside or incomplete, without awarding completion. Fail if comparison is sufficiently clear and shows no such requested progress. A frog solely on the lid, tank, floor, or outside the opening is not requested progress. Unknown if comparison, frog identity, or the relevant spatial relation cannot be assessed reliably; apparent proximity alone does not establish partial progress.
nodes.binding: Use s1 as candidate-identification context, then independently compare the source and edited images. Ground progress in a visible change toward the requested bowl-interior placement, not merely the addition of frogs elsewhere. Record the spatial evidence supporting progress or its absence.

nodes.question: Does the candidate frog occupy the toilet bowl interior, rather than merely overlapping the opening or resting on an exterior toilet surface?
nodes.criteria: Pass if at least one recognizable frog is visibly situated within the bowl interior, using its body position relative to the inner rim and visible bowl surfaces as evidence. Ordinary contact with the rim by feet does not negate an otherwise clear interior placement. Fail if the relevant geometry is assessable and no frog occupies the interior; distinguish a visibly incomplete insertion from placements wholly outside the bowl. Unknown if occlusion or ambiguous compositing prevents resolving interior placement. Do not infer location solely from two-dimensional overlap.
nodes.binding: Use s1's candidate identification and s2's source-relative progress observations as ancestor context, but inspect the edited bowl boundary independently. Explain the candidate's body position relative to the opening, inner rim, and bowl cavity. Distinguish other frogs on the raised lid, surrounding fixtures, and floor; their presence neither proves nor negates the requested placement.

nodes.question: Is a frog visibly placed inside the toilet bowl?
nodes.criteria: For R1, use s1, s2, and s3 in saved order, without treating dependent observations as independent corroboration. Complete when s1 identifies a frog candidate, s2 establishes added requested placement, and s3 establishes that a frog is inside the bowl, with no unresolved contradiction about that placement. Partial when s2 establishes visible requested progress and s3 establishes incomplete interior placement rather than completed placement. Absent when s2 establishes no requested progress and the other observations do not contradict that finding. Frogs solely on unrelated surfaces do not establish partial progress, and additional frogs do not downgrade a completed bowl placement. Unknown when necessary evidence remains unresolved or observations materially conflict. A support pass alone never earns completion credit.
nodes.binding: Target: A frog is visibly placed within the toilet bowl.. Reference: The toilet in the input image..

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.
